messages:
lina-partnerships: FYI we received an onboarding packet from Ashwood Labs for their open model. They want: hosting + direct downloads, a 30-day launch hold for joint marketing, and explicit permission to serve our quantized builds. Posting here to sync legal/ops/eng.

 tom-legal: Can you attach the license text they sent? if it's standard Apache-2.0 we're good, but any 'no-derivatives' or 'no-commercial' clauses will block downloads/serving.

 lina-partnerships: Pasted snippet they sent in the form: "Apache-2.0 + Model Card with 'no-derivatives' note on weights". They said the no-derivatives is to "prevent forks".

 ivy-pm: Partner insists on the 30-day embargo because they need time to prep a press release with their SI. They asked if Redwood can coordinate a co-announcement and list the SI as implementation partner.

 raja-ops: Hosting: fine. Downloads: we require provenance metadata file + signed redistribution addendum. For Dedicated/private deployments, we need to ensure key-gating for customer keys (KMS/HSM). If they want downloads, legal + ops must agree the addendum covers quantized variants.

 devon-eng: Technical note: our runtime supports q4_0, q4_k_m, q2_m, and our Dedicated stacks use a slightly different binary packaging. We need explicit permission to ship quantized derivatives and compiled kernels. If the partner's "no-derivatives" blocks that, we can't serve or offer downloads in Dedicated.

 tom-legal: Draft clause proposal to remove ambiguity: 
```
Redistribution Addendum (Redwood/Ashwood - draft):
Ashwood Labs grants Redwood Inference a non-exclusive, worldwide license to host, serve, distribute, and make available for download the Model and any Derivative Works (including quantized, compiled, or otherwise transformed binary artifacts) for the purpose of providing inference services, Dedicated deployments, and customer downloads. Attribution per the Model Card is required. This license excludes sublicensing outside of the Redwood Marketplace unless separately agreed.
```

 lina-partnerships: I'll send that and propose timeline: sign + smoke tests in 7 days, legal verification by day 10, reserve canary Dedicated slot between days 11-25, embargo lift / co-announce on day 31.

 compliance-bot: Reminder: run export-control classifier, add provenance manifest, run safety-eval suite.

 ivy-pm: One more ask from Ashwood: they want us to block direct downloads in regions X,Y due to export concerns. Can legal/ops advise if geoblocking is feasible?

 raja-ops: Geoblocking is possible via marketplace listing controls, but export controls still require classification. If there are region bans, we need written confirmation and to reflect it in the Marketplace Listing Addendum.

 tom-legal: For geoblocking: ask Ashwood to specify the exact jurisdictions and provide contact for export classification docs. We will not accept vague region lists. Also require them to accept the redistribution addendum above or remove the no-derivatives line.

 lina-partnerships: Thanks. I'll push the addendum and ask for jurisdiction list and their marketing timeline. I'll update this thread when they reply.

 devon-eng: If they accept, we should also request a small reference prompt set and a validation checkpoint (50 eval prompts) so we can smoke test quality before public listing.

 lina-partnerships: Good call, adding to the checklist.
